content:
I noticed that mul_right_cancel_iff and mul_left_cancel_iff have counterparts that make the shared factor an explicit parameter, which makes it easier to specify in a rewrite that you want to left- or right-multiply both sides of an equation by something.

( docs#mul_right_cancel_iff ; docs#mul_left_inj )

There are two things about this that I find surprising.

One, the _inj theorems appear to be specifically designed for the task of rewriting a = b into a * c = b * c, but they are stated "the wrong way around"; using them this way always requires rw [←]. They're better suited to rewriting a * c = b * c into a = b, but for that case they have no special advantage over the _cancel_iffs

Two, their names are mirrored. mul_left_cancel_iff is the same theorem as mul_right_inj and mul_left_inj is the same theorem as mul_right_cancel_iff. I understand the thought behind the naming of the _cancel_iff theorems: multiplying two equal things on the left (or right) by a constant means the constant can be canceled.

But I don't follow the logic of the _inj names. mul_right_inj would seem to suggest "right multiplication is injective", meaning that f(a)=f(b)→a=bf(a) = f(b) \to a = bf(a)=f(b)→a=b, where the function in question is right multiplication, f(a)=acf(a) = acf(a)=ac for some ccc. But this theorem is actually named mul_left_inj; mul_right_inj is the theorem that left-multiplication is injective.

Does anyone have more insight into this?
See #mathlib4 > left and right; it's confusing and there are many inconsistencies

Also the two theorems you mentioned look like duplicates and might not be intentional, even though the bindings differ.
See #mathlib4 > duplicate declarations. We now have a tool to detect dups, but not much progress was made into removing them yet.

Mathlib usually prefers the LHS to be "more complicated" than the RHS, and use implicit params in iff theorems. I agree a flipped version with an explicit param might make sense, but an occasional ← foo (a := 3) isn't so bad compared to duplicating a bunch of lemmas.
It seems that mul_left_inj is used ~100 times, and mul_right_cancel_iff less than 10 times, so I'd guess a PR that removes mul_right_cancel_iff would be welcome
That's sad, considering mul_right_cancel_iff is the one that knows which side of an operator is the left and which is the right. :oh_no:

I think mul_left_inj could (and in my opinion, should) be renamed to mul_const_inj and it could have mul_const_cancel_iff as an alias for discoverability. In generaly, I think we should move to const instead of left/right wherever possible.

These lemmas have two versions depending on whether multiplication occurs on the left or on the right, what would be the name for the other side from mul_const_inj? (I read mul_left_inj a as "multiplication by a on the left is injective" - which BTW would be a more natural name for an implication than an equivalence, but then if the intended use is as a rewriting lemma, why not)
(And then my mind is severely twisted when it turns out that mul_left_inj a actually says that multiplying by a on the right is injective)

Philippe Duchon said:

what would be the name for the other side from mul_const_inj?

const_mul_inj, see the linked left/right thread
OK, so similar to mul_one and one_mul. I get it (but when I cliked on the left/right link I got an error message)
When clicking on #mathlib4 > left and right? What error are you seeing?
I first got an error 404, but then I tried again and found the thread.
